question: What does “آب” (āb) mean?
explanation: “آب” (āb) means “water”. “bread” is نان (nān) and “rice” is برنج (berenj). Literally: yek livān āb mikhāham. = “one glass water want-I”.

question: What does “نان” (nān) mean?
explanation: “نان” (nān) means “bread”. “rice” is برنج (berenj) and “cheese” is پنیر (panir). Literally: nān-e tāze dust dāram. = “bread-of fresh friend have-I (= I like fresh bread)”.

question: What does “برنج” (berenj) mean?
explanation: “برنج” (berenj) means “rice (uncooked)”. “tea” is چای (chāy) and “meat” is گوشت (gusht). Cooked rice is پلو (polo). Literally: berenj va morgh mikhoram. = “rice and chicken eat-I”.

question: What does “چای” (chāy) mean?
explanation: “چای” (chāy) means “tea”. “coffee” is قهوه (ghahve) and “juice” is آب‌میوه (ābmive). Literally: yek chāy mikhāham. = “one tea want-I”.

question: What does “شیر” (shir) mean?
explanation: “شیر” (shir) means “milk”. “yoghurt” is ماست (māst) and “cheese” is پنیر (panir). Shir also means “lion” and “water tap”, so context matters. Literally: shir-e garm mikhoram. = “milk-of warm eat-I”.

question: What does “سیب” (sib) mean?
explanation: “سیب” (sib) means “apple”. “pear” is گلابی (golābi) and “grape” is انگور (angur). Literally: man sib dust dāram. = “I apple friend have-I (= I like apples)”.

question: What does “گربه” (gorbe) mean?
explanation: “گربه” (gorbe) means “cat”. “dog” is سگ (sag) and “bird” is پرنده (parande). Literally: gorbe ru-ye miz ast. = “cat on table is”.

question: What does “سگ” (sag) mean?
explanation: “سگ” (sag) means “dog”. “horse” is اسب (asb) and “fish” is ماهی (māhi). Literally: sag-e man bozorg ast. = “dog-of me big is”.

question: What does “خانه” (khāne) mean?
explanation: “خانه” (khāne) means “house / home”. “door” is در (dar) and “window” is پنجره (panjare). Literally: khāne-ye mā kuchak ast. = “house-of us small is”.

question: What does “در” (dar) mean?
explanation: “در” (dar) means “door”. “wall” is دیوار (divār) and “window” is پنجره (panjare). Dar also means “in”. Literally: dar rā bebband. = “door OBJ close!”.

question: What does “میز” (miz) mean?
explanation: “میز” (miz) means “table”. “chair” is صندلی (sandali) and “bed” is تخت (takht). Literally: ghazā ru-ye miz ast. = “food on table is”.

question: What does “صندلی” (sandali) mean?
explanation: “صندلی” (sandali) means “chair”. “lamp” is چراغ (cherāgh) and “carpet” is فرش (farsh). Literally: ru-ye sandali benshin. = “on chair sit!”.

question: What does “کتاب” (ketāb) mean?
explanation: “کتاب” (ketāb) means “book”. “pen” is خودکار (khodkār) and “notebook” is دفتر (daftar). Literally: in ketāb khub ast. = “this book good is”.

question: What does “خودکار” (khodkār) mean?
explanation: “خودکار” (khodkār) means “pen (ballpoint)”. “pencil” is مداد (medād) and “eraser” is پاک‌کن (pāk-kon). Literally: khodkār dāri? = “pen have-you?”.

question: What does “مدرسه” (madrese) mean?
explanation: “مدرسه” (madrese) means “school”. “university” is دانشگاه (dāneshgāh) and “hospital” is بیمارستان (bimārestān). Literally: madrese sā'at-e hasht shoru' mishavad. = “school hour-of eight start becomes”.

question: What does “دانشگاه” (dāneshgāh) mean?
explanation: “دانشگاه” (dāneshgāh) means “university”. “school” is مدرسه (madrese) and “library” is کتابخانه (ketābkhāne). Literally: u dar dāneshgāh dars mikhānad. = “he/she in university lesson reads (= studies)”.

question: What does “مغازه” (maghāze) mean?
explanation: “مغازه” (maghāze) means “shop”. “bank” is بانک (bānk) and “park” is پارک (pārk). Literally: maghāze bāz ast. = “shop open is”.

question: What does “بیمارستان” (bimārestān) mean?
explanation: “بیمارستان” (bimārestān) means “hospital”. “school” is مدرسه (madrese) and “restaurant” is رستوران (restorān). Literally: bimārestān dur ast. = “hospital far is”.

question: What does “رستوران” (restorān) mean?
explanation: “رستوران” (restorān) means “restaurant”. “hotel” is هتل (hotel) and “museum” is موزه (muze). Literally: in restorān khub ast. = “this restaurant good is”.

question: What does “دوست” (dust) mean?
explanation: “دوست” (dust) means “friend”. “neighbour” is همسایه (hamsāye) and “teacher” is معلم (mo'allem). Dust dāshtan (“to have as a friend”) means “to like”. Literally: u dust-e man ast. = “he/she friend-of me is”.

question: What does “مادر” (mādar) mean?
explanation: “مادر” (mādar) means “mother”. “father” is پدر (pedar) and “sister” is خواهر (khāhar). Literally: mādar-e man mo'allem ast. = “mother-of me teacher is”.

question: What does “پدر” (pedar) mean?
explanation: “پدر” (pedar) means “father”. “son / boy” is پسر (pesar) and “daughter / girl” is دختر (dokhtar). Literally: pedaram kār mikonad. = “father-my work does”.

question: What does “برادر” (barādar) mean?
explanation: “برادر” (barādar) means “brother”. “sister” is خواهر (khāhar) and “uncle” is عمو (amu). Literally: man yek barādar dāram. = “I one brother have-I”.

question: What does “قرمز” (ghermez) mean?
explanation: “قرمز” (ghermez) means “red”. “blue” is آبی (ābi) and “green” is سبز (sabz). Literally: māshin ghermez ast. = “car red is”.

question: What does “آبی” (ābi) mean?
explanation: “آبی” (ābi) means “blue”. “yellow” is زرد (zard) and “black” is سیاه (siyāh). Ābi comes from āb (water). Literally: āsemān ābi ast. = “sky blue is”.

question: What does “سفید” (sefid) mean?
explanation: “سفید” (sefid) means “white”. “black” is سیاه (siyāh) and “grey” is خاکستری (khākestari). Literally: barf sefid ast. = “snow white is”.

question: What does “بزرگ” (bozorg) mean?
explanation: “بزرگ” (bozorg) means “big”. “small” is کوچک (kuchak) and “cold” is سرد (sard). Literally: shahr bozorg ast. = “city big is”.

question: What does “کوچک” (kuchak) mean?
explanation: “کوچک” (kuchak) means “small”. “tall / high” is بلند (boland) and “fast” is سریع (sari'). Literally: otāgh kuchak ast. = “room small is”.

question: What does “گرم” (garm) mean?
explanation: “گرم” (garm) means “warm / hot”. “cold” is سرد (sard) and “wet” is خیس (khis). Literally: emruz havā garm ast. = “today weather hot is”.

question: What does “سریع” (sari') mean?
explanation: “سریع” (sari') means “fast”. “slow” is آهسته (āheste) and “heavy” is سنگین (sangin). Literally: ghatār sari' ast. = “train fast is”.

question: What does “زیبا” (zibā) mean?
explanation: “زیبا” (zibā) means “beautiful”. “ugly” is زشت (zesht) and “tired” is خسته (khaste). Literally: in shahr zibā ast. = “this city beautiful is”.

question: What does “گرسنه” (gorosne) mean?
explanation: “گرسنه” (gorosne) means “hungry”. “thirsty” is تشنه (teshne) and “tired” is خسته (khaste). Literally: man gorosne hastam. = “I hungry am-I”.

question: What does “خسته” (khaste) mean?
explanation: “خسته” (khaste) means “tired”. “happy” is خوشحال (khoshhāl) and “sad / upset” is ناراحت (nārāhat). Literally: man kheyli khaste hastam. = “I very tired am-I”.

question: What does “خوشحال” (khoshhāl) mean?
explanation: “خوشحال” (khoshhāl) means “happy”. “sad” is غمگین (ghamgin) and “angry” is عصبانی (asabāni). Literally: az didan-e shomā khoshhālam. = “from seeing-of you happy-I-am (= nice to see you)”.

question: What does “خوردن” (khordan) mean?
explanation: “خوردن” (khordan) means “to eat”. “to read” is خواندن (khāndan) and “to sleep” is خوابیدن (khābidan). Khordan is also used for drinking tea, water, etc. Literally: sobhāne mikhoram. = “breakfast eat-I”.

question: What does “رفتن” (raftan) mean?
explanation: “رفتن” (raftan) means “to go”. “to come” is آمدن (āmadan) and “to stay” is ماندن (māndan). Literally: be khāne miravam. = “to house go-I”.

question: What does “دیدن” (didan) mean?
explanation: “دیدن” (didan) means “to see”. “to hear” is شنیدن (shenidan) and “to write” is نوشتن (neveshtan). Literally: film rā mibinam. = “film OBJ see-I”.

question: What does “خواندن” (khāndan) mean?
explanation: “خواندن” (khāndan) means “to read”. “to write” is نوشتن (neveshtan) and “to say” is گفتن (goftan). Khāndan also means “to sing” and “to call”. Literally: ketāb mikhānam. = “book read-I”.

question: What does “نوشتن” (neveshtan) mean?
explanation: “نوشتن” (neveshtan) means “to write”. “to read” is خواندن (khāndan) and “to run” is دویدن (davidan). Literally: nāme minevisam. = “letter write-I”.

question: What does “صبحانه” (sobhāne) mean?
explanation: “صبحانه” (sobhāne) means “breakfast”. “lunch” is ناهار (nāhār) and “dinner” is شام (shām). Literally: sobhāne sā'at-e haft ast. = “breakfast hour-of seven is”.

question: What does “اتوبوس” (otobus) mean?
explanation: “اتوبوس” (otobus) means “bus”. “train” is قطار (ghatār) and “plane” is هواپیما (havāpeymā). Literally: otobus dir miyāyad. = “bus late comes”.

question: What does “قطار” (ghatār) mean?
explanation: “قطار” (ghatār) means “train”. “taxi” is تاکسی (tāksi) and “metro” is مترو (metro). Literally: ghatār be tehrān miravad. = “train to Tehran goes”.

question: What does “فرودگاه” (forudgāh) mean?
explanation: “فرودگاه” (forudgāh) means “airport”. “station / stop” is ایستگاه (istgāh) and “port” is بندر (bandar). Literally: forudgāh nazdik ast. = “airport near is”.

question: What does “شهر” (shahr) mean?
explanation: “شهر” (shahr) means “city”. “village” is روستا (rustā) and “street” is خیابان (khiyābān). Literally: tehrān shahr-e bozorgi ast. = “Tehran city-of big is”.

question: What does “دکتر” (doktor) mean?
explanation: “دکتر” (doktor) means “doctor”. “teacher” is معلم (mo'allem) and “driver” is راننده (rānande). Literally: doktor mehrabān ast. = “doctor kind is”.

question: What does “پول” (pul) mean?
explanation: “پول” (pul) means “money”. “price” is قیمت (gheymat) and “card” is کارت (kārt). Literally: pul nadāram. = “money not-have-I”.

question: What does “گران” (gerān) mean?
explanation: “گران” (gerān) means “expensive”. “cheap” is ارزان (arzān) and “free of charge” is رایگان (rāygān). Literally: in kheyli gerān ast. = “this very expensive is”.

question: What does “باران” (bārān) mean?
explanation: “باران” (bārān) means “rain”. “snow” is برف (barf) and “wind” is باد (bād). Literally: bārān miyāyad. = “rain comes”.

question: What does “سر” (sar) mean?
explanation: “سر” (sar) means “head”. “hand” is دست (dast) and “foot / leg” is پا (pā). Literally: saram dard mikonad. = “head-my pain does (= I have a headache)”.

question: What does “دست” (dast) mean?
explanation: “دست” (dast) means “hand”. “eye” is چشم (cheshm) and “ear” is گوش (gush). Literally: dastam dard mikonad. = “hand-my pain does (= my hand hurts)”.

question: What does “سلام” (salām) mean?
explanation: “سلام” (salām) means “Hello”. “Goodbye” is خداحافظ (khodāhāfez) and “Thank you” is مرسی (mersi). Literally: salām, hāl-e shomā chetor ast? = “peace, state-of you how is”.

question: What does “مرسی” (mersi) mean?
explanation: “مرسی” (mersi) means “Thanks”. “Please” is لطفاً (lotfan) and “Sorry” is ببخشید (bebakhshid). Mersi is borrowed from French; ممنون (mamnun) is also “thanks”. Literally: mersi az komaket. = “thanks from help-your”.

question: What does “ببخشید” (bebakhshid) mean?
explanation: “ببخشید” (bebakhshid) means “Excuse me / Sorry”. “Thanks” is مرسی (mersi) and “Please” is لطفاً (lotfan). Literally: bebakhshid, istgāh kojāst? = “forgive, station where-is”.

question: What does “لطفاً” (lotfan) mean?
explanation: “لطفاً” (lotfan) means “Please”. “Welcome” is خوش آمدید (khosh āmadid) and “Yes” is بله (bale). Literally: lotfan āheste sohbat konid. = “please slowly talk do-you”.

question: What does “صبح بخیر” (sobh bekheyr) mean?
explanation: “صبح بخیر” (sobh bekheyr) means “Good morning”. “Good evening” is عصر بخیر ('asr bekheyr) and “Good night” is شب بخیر (shab bekheyr). Literally: sobh bekheyr = “morning to-good”.

question: What does “شب بخیر” (shab bekheyr) mean?
explanation: “شب بخیر” (shab bekheyr) means “Good night”. “Good morning” is صبح بخیر (sobh bekheyr) and “Goodbye” is خداحافظ (khodāhāfez). Literally: shab bekheyr = “night to-good”.

question: What does “خداحافظ” (khodāhāfez) mean?
explanation: “خداحافظ” (khodāhāfez) means “Goodbye”. “Hello” is سلام (salām) and “Thank you” is مرسی (mersi). Literally: khodāhāfez = “God protector”.

question: What does “حال شما چطور است؟” (hāl-e shomā chetor ast?) mean?
explanation: “حال شما چطور است؟” (hāl-e shomā chetor ast?) means “How are you? (formal)”. “What's your name?” is اسم شما چیست؟ (esm-e shomā chist?) and “Where are you from?” is اهل کجا هستید؟ (ahl-e kojā hastid?). Literally: hāl-e shomā chetor ast? = “state-of you how is”.

question: What does “اسمت چیه؟” (esmet chiye?) mean?
explanation: “اسمت چیه؟” (esmet chiye?) means “What's your name? (informal, spoken)”. “How old are you?” is چند سالته؟ (chand sālete?) and “Where do you live?” is کجا زندگی می‌کنی؟ (kojā zendegi mikoni?). Literally: esmet chiye? = “name-your what-is”.

question: What does “اهل کجا هستی؟” (ahl-e kojā hasti?) mean?
explanation: “اهل کجا هستی؟” (ahl-e kojā hasti?) means “Where are you from?”. “Where are you going?” is کجا می‌روی؟ (kojā miravi?) and “What do you do?” is چه کار می‌کنی؟ (che kār mikoni?). Literally: ahl-e kojā hasti? = “native-of where are-you”.

question: What does “نمی‌فهمم” (nemifahmam) mean?
explanation: “نمی‌فهمم” (nemifahmam) means “I don't understand”. “I don't know” is نمی‌دانم (nemidānam) and “I don't want” is نمی‌خواهم (nemikhāham). Literally: nemifahmam = “not-understand-I”.

question: What does “خواهش می‌کنم” (khāhesh mikonam) mean?
explanation: “خواهش می‌کنم” (khāhesh mikonam) means “You're welcome (also: please)”. “Thanks” is مرسی (mersi) and “Goodbye” is خداحافظ (khodāhāfez). Literally: khāhesh mikonam = “request I-do”.

question: What does “این چقدر است؟” (in cheghadr ast?) mean?
explanation: “این چقدر است؟” (in cheghadr ast?) means “How much is this?”. “What is this?” is این چیست؟ (in chist?) and “Where is this?” is این کجاست؟ (in kojāst?). Literally: in cheghadr ast? = “this how-much is”.

question: What does “دستشویی کجاست؟” (dastshuyi kojāst?) mean?
explanation: “دستشویی کجاست؟” (dastshuyi kojāst?) means “Where is the toilet?”. “Where is the station?” is ایستگاه کجاست؟ (istgāh kojāst?) and “What time is it?” is ساعت چند است؟ (sā'at chand ast?). Literally: dastshuyi kojāst? = “toilet where-is”.

question: What does “انگلیسی صحبت می‌کنید؟” (engelisi sohbat mikonid?) mean?
explanation: “انگلیسی صحبت می‌کنید؟” (engelisi sohbat mikonid?) means “Do you speak English?”. “Do you speak Persian?” is فارسی صحبت می‌کنید؟ (fārsi sohbat mikonid?) and “Do you understand?” is متوجه می‌شوید؟ (motavajjeh mishavid?). Literally: engelisi sohbat mikonid? = “English talk do-you”.

question: What does “نوش جان!” (nush-e jān!) mean?
explanation: “نوش جان!” (nush-e jān!) means “Bon appétit! (said to someone eating)”. “Cheers!” is به سلامتی (be salāmati) and “Welcome” is خوش آمدید (khosh āmadid). Literally: nush-e jān! = “nectar-of soul”.

question: What does “تولدت مبارک!” (tavalodet mobārak!) mean?
explanation: “تولدت مبارک!” (tavalodet mobārak!) means “Happy birthday!”. “Happy Nowruz” is نوروز مبارک (nowruz mobārak) and “Welcome” is خوش آمدید (khosh āmadid). Literally: tavalodet mobārak! = “birth-your blessed”.

question: What does “کمک!” (komak!) mean?
explanation: “کمک!” (komak!) means “Help!”. “Stop!” is ایست (ist) and “Fire!” is آتش (ātash). Literally: komak! = “help”.

question: What does “هفت” (haft) mean?
explanation: “هفت” (haft) means “seven”. “six” is شش (shesh) and “eight” is هشت (hasht). Haft (seven) looks like hafte (هفته, week). Literally: yek hafte haft ruz dārad. = “one week seven day has”.

question: What does “بیست” (bist) mean?
explanation: “بیست” (bist) means “twenty”. “ten” is ده (dah) and “thirty” is سی (si). Literally: bist sāl dāram. = “twenty year have-I (= I'm 20)”.

question: What does “صد” (sad) mean?
explanation: “صد” (sad) means “one hundred”. “one thousand” is هزار (hezār) and “ten” is ده (dah). Literally: sad nafar āmadand. = “hundred person came”.

question: What does “دوشنبه” (doshanbe) mean?
explanation: “دوشنبه” (doshanbe) means “Monday”. “Tuesday” is سه‌شنبه (seshanbe) and “Sunday” is یکشنبه (yekshanbe). The Iranian week starts on Saturday (شنبه, shanbe). Literally: doshanbe be madrese miravam. = “Monday to school go-I”.

question: What does “جمعه” (jom'e) mean?
explanation: “جمعه” (jom'e) means “Friday”. “Thursday” is پنجشنبه (panjshanbe) and “Saturday” is شنبه (shanbe). Friday is the main weekend day in Iran. Literally: jom'e ta'til ast. = “Friday holiday is”.

question: What does “دیروز” (diruz) mean?
explanation: “دیروز” (diruz) means “yesterday”. “today” is امروز (emruz) and “tomorrow” is فردا (fardā). Literally: diruz bārān āmad. = “yesterday rain came”.

question: What does “ساعت” (sā'at) mean?
explanation: “ساعت” (sā'at) means “hour / clock / o'clock”. “minute” is دقیقه (daghighe) and “day” is روز (ruz). Literally: sā'at chand ast? = “hour how-many is”.

question: What does “صبح” (sobh) mean?
explanation: “صبح” (sobh) means “morning”. “evening” is عصر ('asr) and “night” is شب (shab). Literally: sobh zud bidār mishavam. = “morning early awake become-I”.

question: What does “او” (u) mean?
explanation: Persian has no grammatical gender, so او (u) means both “he” and “she”. “We” is ما (mā) and “they” is آن‌ها (ānhā). Literally: u dāneshju ast. = “he/she student is”.

question: What does “شما” (shomā) mean?
explanation: شما (shomā) is the polite “you” and also the plural “you”. “I” is من (man) and “he/she” is او (u). Literally: shomā mo'allem hastid? = “you teacher are-you”.

question: How do you say “She is a student”?
explanation: For he/she/it the verb is است (ast). هستم (hastam) goes with “I” and هستند (hastand) with “they”. Literally: u dāneshju ast. = “he/she student is”.

question: Complete: “من دانشجو ___.” (man dāneshju ___.) (I am a student)
explanation: Present of “to be”: هستم (hastam) I am, هستی (hasti) you are, است (ast) he/she is, هستیم (hastim) we are. Literally: man dāneshju hastam. = “I student am-I”.

question: What is the plural of “کتاب” (ketāb, book)?
explanation: The normal plural ending is ها (-hā). The ending ان (-ān) is mostly used for people, e.g. دانشجویان (students). Literally: ketāb-hā ru-ye miz hastand. = “books on table are”.

question: How do you say “two books”?
explanation: After a number the noun stays singular. Literally: do ketāb dāram. = “two book have-I”.

question: How do you say “my book”?
explanation: The possessor follows the noun, linked by an unwritten -e (ezāfe): ketāb-e man. “من کتاب” would be “I book” and “کتاب به من” means “book to me”. Literally: ketāb-e man ru-ye miz ast. = “book-of me on table is”.

question: What does “خانه‌ام” (khāne-am) mean?
explanation: The suffix ـم (-am) means “my”, ـت (-at) “your” and ـش (-ash) “his/her”: خانه‌ات (khāne-at) = your house, خانه‌اش (khāne-ash) = his/her house. Literally: khāne-am bozorg ast. = “house-my big is”.

question: What does “کتابش” (ketābash) mean?
explanation: The suffix ـش (-ash) means “his/her”. My book is کتابم (ketābam) and your book is کتابت (ketābat). Literally: ketābash khub ast. = “book-his/her good is”.

question: Which sentence has the natural word order for “I eat an apple”?
explanation: Persian is subject–object–verb: the verb comes last. Literally: man sib mikhoram. = “I apple eat-I”.

question: Complete: “تو چای ___.” (to chāy ___.) (You drink tea)
explanation: Present = می‌ + stem + ending: می‌خورم (I), می‌خوری (you), می‌خورد (he/she). Khordan is used for “drinking” tea too. Literally: to chāy mikhori. = “you tea eat-you”.

question: Complete: “او به مدرسه ___.” (u be madrese ___.) (She goes to school)
explanation: می‌رود (miravad) = he/she goes, می‌روم (miravam) = I go, می‌روید (miravid) = you (formal/plural) go. Literally: u be madrese miravad. = “he/she to school goes”.

question: How do you say “I went”?
explanation: Past = past stem رفت (raft) + ending: رفتم (raftam). می‌روم means “I go” and خواهم رفت means “I will go”. Literally: man diruz be madrese raftam. = “I yesterday to school went-I”.

question: How do you say “I ate”?
explanation: The past stem of خوردن is خورد (khord), so “I ate” is خوردم (khordam). می‌خورم = I eat; خواهم خورد = I will eat. Literally: nāhār khordam. = “lunch ate-I”.

question: What does “فردا می‌روم” (fardā miravam) mean?
options: I'm going / I will go tomorrow
explanation: Spoken Persian often uses the present tense for the near future. The formal future is خواهم رفت (khāham raft). Literally: fardā miravam. = “tomorrow go-I”.

question: How do you say “I don't want”?
explanation: Add the negative prefix نـ (ne-) before می‌: نمی‌خواهم (nemikhāham). می‌خواهم = I want; خواستم = I wanted. Literally: chāy nemikhāham. = “tea not-want-I”.

question: How do you say “I have a dog”?
explanation: “Have” is دارم (dāram) from داشتن. هستم means “I am” (so the second option says “I am a dog”) and نیستم means “I am not”. Literally: man yek sag dāram. = “I one dog have-I”.

question: How do you say “I like tea”?
explanation: “To like” is دوست داشتن (dust dāshtan), literally “to have as a friend”. The third option means “I have tea”. Literally: man chāy dust dāram. = “I tea friend have-I”.

question: How do you say “She is not here”?
explanation: نیست (nist) is the negative of است (ast). Other forms: نیستم (I'm not), نیستند (they aren't). Literally: u injā nist. = “he/she here isn't”.

question: What does “کجا” (kojā) mean?
explanation: کجا (kojā) = where, چرا (cherā) = why, چطور (chetor) = how. Literally: kojā miravi? = “where go-you”.

question: What does “چند” (chand) mean?
explanation: چند (chand) asks for numbers or amounts. “Why” is چرا and “where” is کجا. Literally: chand nafar hastid? = “how-many person are-you”.

question: Complete: “من ___ ایران هستم.” (man ___ irān hastam.) (I am from Iran)
explanation: از (az) = from, به (be) = to, با (bā) = with. Literally: man az irān hastam. = “I from Iran am-I”.

question: What is the job of “را” (rā) in “کتاب را می‌خوانم” (ketāb rā mikhānam)?
options: It marks a specific (definite) direct object
explanation: را (rā) follows a definite direct object: “I'm reading the book”. Without it, کتاب می‌خوانم means “I read books” in general. “And” is و (va) and “with” is با (bā). Literally: ketāb rā mikhānam. = “book OBJ read-I”.

question: What does “نان هست؟” (nān hast?) mean?
explanation: هست (hast) expresses existence or availability; the negative is نیست (nist). “Is the bread fresh?” would be نان تازه است؟ and “Where is the bread?” is نان کجاست؟. Literally: nān hast? = “bread is?”.
